answer: A verifiable delay mechanism deters Sybil attacks by registering sequential time-lock proofs on a shared atlas. Maintaining validity requires proving a continuous latency delta between cryptographic pulses, forcing an adversary to expend dedicated, non-parallelizable CPU core time per identity. When an attacker's compute capacity hits its nadir, surplus identities desynchronize and expire. However, this constant calculation wastes energy and penalizes low-power edge devices.
